gaps: The direct official Unihan records for 課 and 果 returned internal errors. Current Mandarin readings were not verified from the required official character records; the secondary 課 page gives kè, and the 果 page search result gives guǒ, but these are not equivalent evidence.

The local Baxter–Sagart file contains a 果 row (row 1181) but no 課 row. Its 果 reconstruction is `*[k]ˤo[r]ʔ`; no same-system local host reading could be compared. Do not merge its notation with Zhengzhang readings in the dossier.
The opened Academia Sinica page did not render the character's historical glyph sequence as readable text. Earliest attestation, dated graphic stages, and any corruption hypothesis remain unverified.

《說文》's 試也 analysis and sound-component claim are clear; no independently checked paleographic source confirmed the graphic history or justified the semantic role of 言 beyond its conventional speech-related classifier function.

The early Han citation supports assessment of officials. The chronology and semantic bridge from testing/assessment to taxation, school study, a lesson period, and administrative department remain incompletely established; a dictionary sense list cannot supply that chronology.

No source identified here dates the standardized simplification 課 → 课 or specifically verifies that 言 was reduced to 讠 in this character. The dossier's simplification claim is consistent with modern usage but not independently dated in this search.
No permission/license investigation found a clear basis to create a reusable local extract from recurring sources; no extract is recommended.

No downloadable glyph candidate with verified direct image URL, exact asset rights, and source provenance was established. No image is proposed; a Wiktionary glyph-data module was discovered but not inspected as an asset source.

Earliest attestation of 課 and date of its first graphic appearance remain unestablished. The MOE record lists a Qin text form as unavailable and secondary image labels for Qin/Han materials need primary artifact-level verification.

The sources support the traditional 說文 analysis 从言、果聲 and an early test/examination sense. The precise semantic contribution of 言 beyond conventional speech-related categorization is not independently established.

Assessment and official evaluation are attested in classical sources cited by MOE, including 漢書; this does not date transitions to school lesson/course, tax, or administrative-unit senses. The links among these senses remain partly undocumented.
No ancient graph corruption hypothesis or evidence of corruption emerged. Distinct local Baxter–Sagart notation for 果 cannot be matched against 課 because the dataset contains no 課 row.
Modern kè was reported by the MOE dictionary for 課; modern guǒ for 果 was not verified from official Unihan in this run. These current readings do not establish ancient sound correspondence.
The official Unicode endpoints for U+8AB2 and U+679C failed. The local dataset row supports 果 only and must not be treated as a click-through verification of the official reading.

The official Unicode Unihan character pages for 課 and 果 could not be inspected because both endpoints returned internal errors. Their current readings are supported here by inspected Taiwan MOE dictionary records, while the supplied local Unihan rows are identified only as local evidence.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart data contains 果 but no 課 row, so this evidence set cannot provide a same-system Baxter–Sagart comparison for the phonetic component and host. Keep the dataset notation *[k]ˤo[r]ʔ for 果 distinct from other reconstruction systems.

The source explicitly analyzes traditional 課 as 从言、果聲. This supports 言’s conventional semantic-category role and 果’s phonetic role in 課; it does not independently explain the precise semantic contribution of 言.

A character-specific primary source explicitly documenting the correspondence of 言 to visible 讠 in 课 was not verified. Keep the semantic-component analysis scoped to traditional 課; the whole-character simplified-counterpart relationship is reported in dossier sources but was not independently dated here.

The MOE dictionary reports early evaluation examples, including a 《漢書》 citation, and later educational examples, but this does not establish the exact first attestations or prove the semantic bridge to modern lesson/course meanings. Tax and administrative-section senses likewise remain without a demonstrated chronology.

No readable primary paleographic sequence, earliest graphic attestation, or evidence of corruption was established in this search. The MOE character page lists its Han-slip form as unavailable; no glyph image was visually inspected.

The official Unicode Unihan character endpoints for 課 and 果 were not verified in this invocation. The supplied local kMandarin rows were identified as local provenance; inspected MOE dictionary entries independently confirm the two current readings.

No same-system ancient reconstruction for both 課 and 果 is available in the supplied Baxter–Sagart rows: 果 is *[k]ˤo[r]ʔ and there is no 課 row. Keep that notation distinct from the dossier’s Zhengzhang reconstructions. Modern kè and guǒ do not establish the historical sound relationship.

The traditional 說文 analysis supports 言 and 果 roles in 課. The standardized table independently supports 课〔課〕 and the 言→讠 simplification mapping in this graph, but it does not establish an independent semantic role for 讠 in the simplified form.

No inspected primary paleographic source established 課’s earliest attestation, dated graphic sequence, or a corruption hypothesis. The 《說文》 analysis is a historical dictionary account, not proof of the earliest form.
